sweep_summary: Ocotepec Mixtec (ocot1243) is not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title's single title hit, Rathcke et al. 2021 'Tapping into linguistic rhythm', is a Glottolog computerized mis-assignment (the record says so: language code 'computerized assignment from \"tapping\"', seeded by Mak 1977 'Maguey tapping in the highland Mixteco'); its abstract shows it is an English finger-tapping rhythm-perception study — irrelevant, priority none. Beyond the item I looked for a first-hand stress statement for this language and read nothing that gives one: Eberhardt 1999 'Questions and inversion in Ocotepec Mixtec' (downloaded from the Internet Archive, saved) is syntax only and silent on stress; Mak 1977 'Picturesque Mixtec talk' (Tlalocan, open, saved) has tone puns but no stress statement; WALS has no stress features coded for mxo. The likely best statements remain unread: Alexander 1988 'A syntactic sketch of Ocotepec Mixtec' (SIL; old open URL is dead with no archived copy at the Internet Archive, sil.org blocks our network; Harvard print PM4017.S78 1988) — high priority; Mak 1958 'The tonal system of a third Mixtec dialect' IJAL 24:61-70, doi:10.1086/464433 (paywalled) — medium; Josserand 1983 Mixtec dialect history (Tulane PhD, ProQuest) — medium for the proto-Mixtec couplet-initial stress generalization.

Repositorio CIESAS hdl 1015/1485.
tone_statements.quote: Referente al inventario tonal de la lengua tu’un savi de Ocotepec, Mak (1958:61) describe 9 tonos (1, 2, 3 tonos de nivel y las otras seis posibles combinaciones entre estos, que nos da un total de 9 patrones tonales). En esta investigación realizada en esta misma variante se encuentran, en cambio, 10 tonos (3 de nivel B = bajo, M = medio, A = alto y 7 de contorno AS, AM, AB, MA, MB, BA, BM, donde S = súper alto). [...] En la lengua tu’un savi de Ocotepec el tono también tiene funciones gramaticales. En la Tabla 6, se muestran algunos verbos en que el aspecto completivo se asocia al patrón tonal MB, el incompletivo al patrón MM, y el irrealis al patrón MA.
tone_statements.translation: As to the tonal inventory of the tu'un savi of Ocotepec, Mak (1958:61) describes 9 tones (1, 2, 3 level tones and the other six possible combinations among them, giving 9 tonal patterns in all). In this investigation of the same variety, by contrast, 10 tones are found (3 level: B = low, M = mid, A = high, and 7 contour: AS, AM, AB, MA, MB, BA, BM, where S = super-high). [...] In the tu'un savi of Ocotepec tone also has grammatical functions. Table 6 shows some verbs in which completive aspect is associated with the tonal pattern MB, incompletive with MM, and irrealis with MA.

tone_statements.citation: Hollenbach, Barbara E. 2003. The historical source of an irregular Mixtec tone-sandhi pattern. In Language and life: Essays in memory of Kenneth L. Pike, 533-550. SIL International & UT Arlington.
tone_statements.quote: Ocotepec has sandhi rules that change mid-low words to high-low following certain other words. The words that are changed to high-low include those with the (C)VCV syllable pattern, as well as those with the (C)VꞌV and (C)VV patterns (Mak 1958:65).
tone_statements.check: quotation from the author's open copy, read 2026-09-25; not yet verified by a second reading
tone_statements.summary: Secondary (Mak 1958:63-65). Ocotepec lacks the irregular mid-low → mid-high sandhi; Spanish penultimate-stress loans take high-low (lado → ládo̱, calle → káyi̱, marco → márku̱; ex. 29). Consistent with the catalog tone class lexical-tone; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mak, Cornelia (1958). The tonal system of a third Mixtec dialect. International Journal of American Linguistics 24(1):61-70.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: The ST dialect, in common with SM, has three phonemic tone levels (tonemes). These yield the following possible tone couplets: 1-1, 1-2, 1-3; 2-1, 2-2, 2-3; 3-1, 3-2, 3-3. Each of these nine tone couplets occur in ST. This is in contrast to SM and SE, where the 3-3 (or *4-4 for SE) couplet does not occur.
sources.note: The only phonological description of Ocotepec Mixtec; Alexander 1988 defers to it for the full phonology, and Mak's IJAL tone papers of the 1950s normally open with a segmental/prosodic sketch where a stress remark would sit. Ten pages; SIL record confirms subject language mie.
